messages:
deploybot: scheduled migration 'add_last_seen_col' on user_profiles in change window 2025-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC. running online backfill, estimated runtime 18-25m. canary 2% traffic, pinned service image services/user-service@v3.14.2. holdpoint at 02:10 UTC. automatic rollback if error_rate>1% or p99 latency >200ms for 3m. :information_source:
maria: ack. can we pin DB client lib to 2.8.1 for the canary? last time 2.9 broke the decoder path. also request quiesce for noncritical writes at 02:05-02:12 if possible.
sam: i'm on-call that window, i'll watch replica lag + tx/sec. can we add a row-limit to the backfill so we can throttle faster if needed? suggest chunk_size=250.
liz: +1 to chunk_size. also prefer running FK validation as async check after field add (non-blocking) — avoids long locks.
kevin: rollback plan written: 1) pause backfill 2) revert service pin to services/user-service@v3.14.1 3) run reverse migration job to drop col if needed (idempotent) 4) clear feature-flag. if we hit holdpoint, we do steps 1-2 immediately.
maria: for pinning, add this to release notes / deploy config: `image_pin: "services/user-service@v3.14.2"` and feature flag `user_profiles.last_seen_v2` default off.
deploybot: pause command (manual): `/deploy pause 6172468021`
kevin: monitoring hooks: DB: pg.stat_activity, replica_lag, locks; infra: 95th tail for api-user and p99 latency for user-service. alert thresholds set in runbook.
sam: adding preflight checklist to thread: - confirm client pin deployed to canary - run small canary backfill on staging - verify no long-running locks on staging - ensure read replicas lag < 5s before cutover
liz: minor note: if we see repeated lock waits on the primary, switch to 'prefix-cache' mode for the user-service to avoid hot writes to the affected partitions.
maria: tagging @kevin @sam for holdpoint owners. i'll update the release notes and set the feature flag gating. :thumbsup:
deploybot: noted. will emit a deploybot check-in at T-15m and at holdpoint. will open the thread channel #deploy-6172468021 during the window.
